source_text: Si quis dicit: alius est filius Dei ante saecula, et alius qui extremis temporibus apparuit; et non confitetur unum et eundem esse illum ante saecula, et qui novissimis temporibus apparuit, sicut scriptum est; anathema sit. Quomodo dici potest alius filius Dei ante saecula, et alius in extremis temporibus; cum ipse Dominus dicat: Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum. Et, quia a patre exivi, et venio; et iterum vado ad patrem meum?
thought_title: One Son Before Ages and in Last Times
orientation: Gregory condemns the error that there is one Son of God before the ages and a different Son who appeared in the last times, citing Christ's own words about his pre-existence and origin from the Father.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says: another is son of God before ages, and another who in last times appeared; and not confesses one and same to be that one before ages, and who in last times appeared, as written is; anathema let him be. How can it be said another son of God before ages, and another in last times; since himself the Lord says: Before Abraham was made, I am. And, because from the Father I came forth, and I come; and again I go to my Father?

choices.why: Standard temporal formula for eternal pre-existence; matches the brief's emphasis on eternal existence.
Refers to the final period of salvation history when Christ appeared incarnate.
Synonym for extremis temporibus in the confession clause; rendered identically for consistency.

choices.english: confesses that the same one is he
choices.why: Captures the force of confessing identity (unum et eundem) with the demonstrative 'he' (ille implied).
rejected: confesses one and the same to be
acknowledges one and the same to be

choices.english: Before Abraham came to be, I am
choices.why: Literal rendering of Christ's words (John 8:58); 'fieret' = came to be/was made, 'ego sum' = I am.

choices.term: quia a patre exivi, et venio; et iterum vado ad patrem meum
choices.english: because I went forth from the Father, and I come; and again I go to my Father
choices.why: Preserves the sequence of going forth, coming, and returning; present tense 'exivi' rendered as perfect 'went forth' for English idiom.
rejected: because I came out from the Father, and I come; and again I go to my Father
since I proceeded from the Father, and I am coming; and again I am going to my Father

bible_refs.note: quia a patre exivi, et venio; et iterum vado ad patrem meum

pass_b_english: If anyone says that one is the Son of God before the ages, and another the one who appeared in the last times, and does not confess that the same one is he before the ages and who appeared in the last times, as it is written, let him be anathema. How can it be said that one is the Son of God before the ages, and another in the last times, when the Lord himself says, "Before Abraham came to be, I am"? And, "Because I went forth from the Father, and I come; and again I go to my Father" (John 8:58; John 16:28).
